\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نوبت} (nowbat)}{نوبت (nowbat)}]{\fa{نوبت} (nowbat) — a turn (in a queue); an appointment}

\label{lesson:FA-C452-nobat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a passer-by, then the Persian for someone from the same town.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نوبت}}
\textbf{\fa{نوبت}} (\emph{nowbat}) — \textquotedblleft{}a turn (in a queue); an appointment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{بانک} \fa{باید} \fa{منتظر} \fa{نوبت} \fa{بمانیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar bânk bâyad montazer-e nowbat bemânim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At the bank we have to wait our turn.
\end{quote}

\emph{Nowbat-e shomâst} — it's your turn.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nowbat} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{nawba} 'a turn, a change of the guard' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nowbat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nowbat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{nowbat}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a passer-by, then the Persian for someone from the same town, then say \emph{nowbat} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نوبت} \fa{گرفتن} (nowbat gereftan)}{نوبت گرفتن (nowbat gereftan)}]{\fa{نوبت} \fa{گرفتن} (nowbat gereftan) — to get an appointment; to take a queue number}

\label{lesson:FA-C452-nobat-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for someone from the same town, then the Persian for a turn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نوبت} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{نوبت} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{nowbat gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to get an appointment; to take a queue number\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برای} \fa{دکتر} \fa{از} \fa{هفته} \fa{قبل} \fa{نوبت} \fa{گرفتم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Barâ-ye doktor az hafte-ye qabl nowbat gereftam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I made the doctor's appointment a week ago.
\end{quote}

\emph{nowbat} + \emph{gereftan} 'to take'. Present stem \emph{gir-}: \emph{nowbat migiram}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nowbat gereftan} is built from \emph{nowbat} 'a turn', borrowed from Arabic \emph{nawba} (EtymDB), and the native verb \emph{gereftan} 'to take', usually traced to Old Persian \emph{grab-}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nowbat gereftan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nowbat gereftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{nowbat gereftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for someone from the same town, then the Persian for a turn, then say \emph{nowbat gereftan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{نوبت} \fa{گرفتن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To get an appointment; to take a queue number\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{معطل} \fa{شدن} (mo'attal shodan)}{معطل شدن (mo'attal shodan)}]{\fa{معطل} \fa{شدن} (mo'attal shodan) — to be kept waiting, to be held up}

\label{lesson:FA-C452-moattal-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a turn, then the Persian for to get an appointment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{معطل} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{معطل} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{mo'attal shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be kept waiting, to be held up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{اداره} \fa{دو} \fa{ساعت} \fa{معطل} \fa{شدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar edâre do sâ'at mo'attal shodim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We were kept waiting for two hours at the office.
\end{quote}

\emph{mo'attal} 'idle, waiting' + \emph{shodan}. \emph{Kasi râ mo'attal kardan} — to keep someone waiting.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mo'attal shodan} is built from \emph{mo'attal} 'held up, idle', borrowed from Arabic \emph{muʿaṭṭal}, which EtymDB lists, and the native verb \emph{shodan} 'to become'. It shares its root with \emph{ta'til} 'closure'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mo'attal shodan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mo'attal shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{mo'attal shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a turn, then the Persian for to get an appointment, then say \emph{mo'attal shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{معطل} \fa{شدن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To be kept waiting, to be held up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{فیش} (fish)}{فیش (fish)}]{\fa{فیش} (fish) — a payment slip, a bank receipt}

\label{lesson:FA-C452-fish}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to get an appointment, then the Persian for to be kept waiting.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{فیش}}
\textbf{\fa{فیش}} (\emph{fish}) — \textquotedblleft{}a payment slip, a bank receipt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{فیش} \fa{بانکی} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{منشی} \fa{دادم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Fish-e bânki râ be monshi dâdam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I gave the bank slip to the secretary.
\end{quote}

Offices often ask for a \emph{fish} to show you have paid.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fish} was borrowed from French and is usually traced to French \emph{fiche} 'a slip of paper, an index card'. EtymDB does not list the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fish}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{fish}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to get an appointment, then the Persian for to be kept waiting, then say \emph{fish} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مالیات} (mâliyât)}{مالیات (mâliyât)}]{\fa{مالیات} (mâliyât) — tax}

\label{lesson:FA-C452-maliyat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be kept waiting, then the Persian for a payment slip.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مالیات}}
\textbf{\fa{مالیات}} (\emph{mâliyât}) — \textquotedblleft{}tax\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هر} \fa{سال} \fa{مالیات} \fa{خانه} \fa{را} \fa{میپردازیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Har sâl mâliyât-e khâne râ mipardâzim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Every year we pay the tax on the house.
\end{quote}

An Arabic-shaped plural built on \emph{mâl} 'property'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mâliyât} is an Arabic-shaped plural, usually traced to Arabic \emph{māliyya}, from \emph{māl} 'property, wealth'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to be kept waiting, then the Persian for a payment slip, then say \emph{mâliyât} again
